# 1 Enoch Chapter 56 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 56:2 — 'elect and beloved ones' as the targets of punishment

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their-elect and-beloved-ones" | Literal; the referent is ambiguous — whose elect? |
| LOGOS | "their elect and beloved ones" | Preserves the ambiguity; the elect of the wicked kings |
| PNEUMA | "their chosen and beloved" | 'Chosen' for 'elect'; smooths slightly |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained 'elect and beloved ones' (EMET/LOGOS). The 'their' is intentionally ambiguous in the Ge'ez — it may refer to the elect of the wicked (i.e., the wicked leaders' own followers) now being judged. 'Elect' is preserved throughout the Parables for terminological consistency.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 56:4 — 'Parthians and Medes' — historical identification

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-Parthians and-the-Medes" | Preserved as proper names |
| LOGOS | "the Parthians and the Medes" | Agrees — historical proper nouns |
| PNEUMA | "the Parthians and the Medes" | Agrees; brief contextual note added in translator's note |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three translators agree. 'Parthians and Medes' preserved as the Ge'ez proper nouns. This is one of the clearest historical anchors in the Parables and should not be paraphrased.

**Status:** Full convergence. No dispute.

---

## 56:7 — 'Sheol' vs. 'the grave' vs. 'the underworld'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Sheol" | Preserved untranslated; the Ge'ez she'ol is the Hebrew loanword |
| LOGOS | "Sheol" | Agrees |
| PNEUMA | "Sheol" | Agrees; dynamic note explains as 'the realm of the dead' |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** All three translators preserve 'Sheol' untranslated. Full convergence on this key term.

**Status:** Full convergence.

---

## 56:6 — 'city of my righteous' — whose city?

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-city of-my-righteous" | Literal Ge'ez; the Lord speaks in first person |
| LOGOS | "the city of my righteous" | Agrees with EMET |
| PNEUMA | "the city of my righteous ones" | Minor expansion; 'ones' added for natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The sudden first-person voice ('my righteous') implies the Lord of Spirits is speaking directly, which is significant. PNEUMA's minor addition of 'ones' is acceptable but unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Minor divergence.

---
